content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: no-cost break shifts, IVR callbacks and an extended UPI outage message, predicted to lift service level to 85.5% for 11:30-13:30 against the 80% target.","why":"The surge is driven by the P1 UPI switch incident (INC-20261006-6998). Payments calls hit 213 at 10:30 against 111.9 forecast, and upi_payment_failed calls are running 2.56x normal. Staffing and handle time are fine, so this is a demand problem, not a staffing one. Doing nothing (P0) only just clears the target overall at 80.4%, and general would sit at 71.6%. P1 costs nothing and breaks no policy. It raises the window service level to 85.5% (payments 90.2%, general 78.1%), cuts abandons from 4.8% to 3.5% and lifts rest-of-day to 93.7%. It is the cheapest plan that meets the target.","trade_offs":["General queue stays below 80% at 78.1% under P1. P2 (₹720) brings it to 84.5% and P3 (₹3,960) to 89.0%.","P2 adds chat deflection for ₹720, giving 89.4% overall and 2.9% abandons. That is a modest gain for a small cost if general matters.","P3 overtime for 20 agents gives the best result (91.7%, 1.9% abandons) but costs ₹3,960 and depends on agents accepting the offer.","Delaying breaks by 30-45 minutes puts extra strain on agents during a busy period."],"watch":"Watch the general queue, which is the weak spot at a predicted 78.1%. If it trends lower, or the UPI incident runs past 13:30, consider moving to P2. Keep the outage message in line with incident updates and remove it once UPI recovers. No escalation to the duty manager is needed."}
